newsitem.title: USA: US productivity may rise further-Minn. Fed's Stern.
newsitem.headline: US productivity may rise further-Minn. Fed's Stern.

text.p: The U.S. economy has experienced recent productivity gains and there is a chance it will see further significant improvements in that area, said a top official at the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis.
"I don't see any reason at this point to get negative about productivity," Minneapolis Fed president Gary Stern told members of the American Farm Bureau gathered here for a conference.
"There is a hint there's something more positive going on with productivity. Maybe we can look forward to further significant productivity gains from here," Stern added.
Stern also said that he saw no credit contraints in the U.S. economy, with the exception, maybe, of some tighteness in the consumer credit sector.

"We don't perceive there is any shortage of credit in agricultural or any other sector of the economy. Credit is readily available, but one place where it might be a touch tighter is on the consumer side," Stern said.
"Credit card lenders have gotten more cautions ... We have a lot of competition in financial services. As long as that persists, reasonable credit risk will get financed," he added.
Although the Minneapolis Fed president praised the current economic scenario in the U.S., he said he did not believe the economy had entered a "new era."
"It would be wonderful if we were in a new era, but new eras always come to the same end ... While times are awfully good, I don't think we're in a new era," Stern said.
Many U.S. economists have said they believe the economy has entered a "new era," in which global competition and rising productivity would put a permanent lid on inflation.
